forecaster_note: Mon: peaky waist–chest, clean to cleanish AM with light offshores, some wobbly short-period wind wave; NE'lies pick up later and get lumpy. Tue: weak, waist–chest, S-facing cleanest early. Wed: worth a look in the AM, peaky chest-high, then NE'lies. Thu: longer, better-angled ENE/NE fetch building more size and shape; wind flips south at some point over the weekend. — Surfline forecaster, Mon 19 Oct

wind.summary: Onshore ENE ~15 kph at midday, building to ~21 kph arvo and 23+ kph evening. Was light offshore W/SW (<10 kph) at dawn. Mostly clear, ~20°C.

shark.summary: No shark detections at Palm Beach → Manly in the last 24h (incl. Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl, North Steyne). Feed is current — newest statewide detection ~1h ago (Port Macquarie); ~54 real detections statewide in 24h. Nearest: tagged Bull Shark #969 at Killcare (Central Coast) ~18h ago, outside the Northern Beaches. DPI feed returned no features. Detections are receiver pings, not sightings — still check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Weak mixed swell (~181 kJ): short SE 8s + ENE wind chop. Onshore ENE since midday and building — arvo is poor. Best bet is tomorrow dawn.
days.surfline_text: Some peaky surf about in the waist to chest range. It's clean to cleanish and will stay that way for morning - with light offshore winds - but there's some short period wind wave in the mix and it's a bit wobbly / junky looking.   Later NE'lies pick up and it will get lumpy for most spots - OK for the proper S facing breaks though.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Early read: Wed worth a look at dawn (chest-high, peaky). Surfline flags a longer, better-angled ENE/NE fetch for the weekend with more size and shape, and a southerly change at some point — could give a good morning. Low confidence until Thursday.
days.surfline_text: We should get a bit of a longer better angled fetch and some more size and shape to the ENE / NE swell.   Winds likely start off N/NE but then should flip south at some point in the weekend. That change could give us a good morning of waves.
